'''Frances Harshbarger''' (16 August 1902, [[Quimby, Iowa]] &ndash; 11 February 1987, [[Cuyahoga Falls]], [[Ohio]]) was an American mathematician.<ref name="Green.LaDuke.2009"/>

==Education==
She obtained her [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] with honors in 1923 at [[Grinnell College]],<ref>[http://www.math.grinnell.edu/graduates.xhtml Grinnell graduates list] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180308151514/http://www.math.grinnell.edu/graduates.xhtml |date=2018-03-08 }}, class of 1923</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Green |first1=Judy |last2=LaDuke |first2=Jeanne |title=History of Mathematics, Vol 34: Pioneering Women in American Mathematics: The Pre-1940 PhD's |date=2009 |publisher=American Mathematical Society, London Mathematical Society |location=United States of America |isbn=978-0-8218-4376-5 |page=193 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IRbOAwAAQBAJ&dq=Frances+Harshbarger+grinnell&pg=PA193 |access-date=24 June 2021}}</ref> and went to [[West Virginia University]] to serve as a half-time teacher and simultaneously work on her mathematics graduation; in 1925 she finished her [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] After that she became head of the mathematics department of [[Potomac State College]] in [[Keyser, West Virginia]]. In 1927 to 1929, she was an assistant, in 1929 to 1930 a fellow, at the [[University of Illinois]]. In 1930, she obtained her Ph.D. in mathematics with a thesis in algebraic geometry,<ref>{{cite thesis | type=Ph.D. thesis | author=Frances Harshbarger | title=The Geometric Configuration Defined by a Special Algebraic Relation of Genus Four | institution=University of Illinois | year=1930 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1931-033-02/S0002-9947-1931-1501606-X | author=Frances Harshbarger | title=The Geometric Configuration Defined by a Special Algebraic Relation of Genus Four | journal=[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] | volume=33 | number=2 | pages=557–578 | date=Apr 1931 | doi=10.2307/1989423| jstor=1989423 | doi-access=free }}</ref> advised by [[A. B. Coble]].<ref>{{mathGenealogy|4145}}</ref> She was one of the first American women who obtained a mathematics Ph.D. degree.<ref name="Green.LaDuke.2009">{{cite book | title-link= Pioneering Women in American Mathematics | isbn=978-0-8218-4376-5 | first1 = Judy | last1 = Green | author1-link = Judy Green (mathematician) | first2 = Jeanne | last2 = LaDuke | author2-link = Jeanne LaDuke | title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics &mdash; The Pre-1940 PhD's | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]], The [[London Mathematical Society]] | series=History of Mathematics | volume=34 | edition=1st | date=2009 }} Biography on pp.&nbsp;244 of the [https://www.ams.org/bookpages/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf Supplementary Material] at [https://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34 AMS]</ref>

==Career==
Thereafter, she worked as a professor in the American College for Girls, the university section of [[Robert College]], in [[Istanbul, Turkey]].<ref name="Green.LaDuke.2009"/> She attended the 1932 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Zürich]] as an official delegate.<ref>[http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1932.1/ICM1932.1.ocr.pdf Vol.1] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110225505/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1932.1/ICM1932.1.ocr.pdf |date=2017-11-10 }} of the Congress Proceedings, p. 10, 25 (= p. 18, 33 in the Pdf file)</ref> In 1934, she returned to the United States to teach at the high school associated with the University of Chicago. For the rest of her career, she served at [[Kent State University]] in Ohio, as an appointed instructor since 1935, an assistant professor since 1936, an associate professor since 1942, and a professor since 1946, until she retired in 1972, as emeritus professor.<ref name="Green.LaDuke.2009"/>
